title: ARP
summary: ARP maps IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses inside a local network.

concepts.name: ARP request
concepts.description: An ARP request asks who owns a specific IPv4 address on the local network.

concepts.name: ARP reply
concepts.description: An ARP reply provides the MAC address for the requested IPv4 address.

notes.overview: ARP helps a device find the local MAC address needed to send an IPv4 packet on Ethernet.
notes.core_concept: ARP maps an IPv4 address to a MAC address within the same local network.
notes.explanation: A host broadcasts an ARP request, and the device with that IPv4 address replies with its MAC address.
notes.example: Before sending to 192.168.1.20 on the LAN, a laptop may ask who has that IP address.

common_mistake.content: A common mistake is expecting ARP to work across the internet; ARP works only on the local link.

quick_check.question: What does ARP find for an IPv4 address?
quick_check.answer: The matching MAC address on the local network.

notes.practice_prompt: Describe the two messages involved in resolving an IPv4 address with ARP.
notes.simple_explanation: ARP is like asking everyone in the room who has a certain name tag.
notes.analogy: The ARP cache is like a small contact list of recently found local devices.
notes.advanced_example: A host usually sends packets for remote networks to the default gateway MAC address, not the remote host MAC.
notes.edge_case: If no ARP reply arrives, the host cannot build the Ethernet frame for that local next hop.
notes.challenge_question: Why does a host ARP for the default gateway when the destination IP is outside the local subnet?
